Peter Hilliar judged it even finer. After a scooter breakdown he arrived at the start with only half a minute to spare - good job the start was 6 minutes late!

The B team, with an unfit Peter Hilliar running, were falling back. Tony Fairclough took the fourth leg and kept the lead but Brian Hall of Manchester closed the gap to about thirty seconds and the Lads Club were getting confident of their chances.

Although my subjects are a little older than this, and you may need to watch for rather more than one season, I would commend to my favoured clients the following promising specimens:-John Dear. Peter Hilliar,Dick Calderwood, Ron Sinclair, Doug Brew, Bob James and Joe Riley.

However, a tough week-end at the Merthyr Mawr training camp a few days earlier had taken it out of them and they both experienced one of "those" days, slipping back down the field to 116th and 188th positions, leaving Peter Hilliar (80) and new member Dick Calderwood (110) to close in the team.
Unfortunately, Trevor was the only "top man" present and we had to wait till 56th place for our 2nd scorer, Arthur Bruce. Chris Keavey and Peter Hilliar completed the 'A' team.
On the track John Dear recorded a good 9:37.8 for 4th in the Steeplechase and Peter Hilliar made a welcome return to our trophy team with 3rd in the 'B' 880y.
Meanwhile Hart had retired ("the pace was too fast"), Bill Dance was another to pass the still unfit North and Peter Hilliar was suffering badly with stitch.

There were other good performances by Nick Head (Javelin and Discus), Bob Couillault (Triple), new member Robertson (Hammer), Tony Brooks (400) and Peter Hilliar (800).
Alan Mead and Pete Hilliar both recorded 1:57.4 metres and Tony Brooks 1:58.2 yards. Lionel Mann, a distance runner of repute, also encroached on this event with a 1:58.1 metres.

The 800 metres was an uneven race, only settled down the straight, where Peter Hilliar held off a fast-finishing John Boardman. The first five finishers were within 0.8 second of each other, giving an indication of their closeness.
